Undermine

/un-der-MYN/ — stress on the last syllable · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To undermine something is to gradually weaken it or damage its support, often little by little.

Rumors undermined the manager's authority long before the vote.

Worked Example

For weeks, the rival candidate released stories suggesting the mayor had mismanaged funds, and with each story her credibility with voters slipped away.

The weakening here is deliberate and gradual — each rumor chipped away at her standing, not all at once but little by little from beneath. Undermine is more precise than 'damage' because it captures that slow, hidden weakening of support from underneath, like digging away at a foundation.

How Undermine Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

weaken

weaken: to make something less strong, in any way

sabotage

sabotage: to wreck something on purpose, often secretly

subvert

subvert: to secretly overturn an authority or system

Antonyms

bolster

bolster: to prop up and strengthen something's support

support

support: to hold something up and help it stand

How Strong Is It? — doubt → weaken → demolish → undermine

doubt vs. undermine

doubt vs. undermine: Doubt is only a seed compared with undermine: to doubt a leader is to question her privately, while to undermine her is to quietly chip away at her actual support.

weaken vs. undermine

weaken vs. undermine: Weaken is broader and often milder than undermine; anything can weaken something openly, but to undermine is to weaken it from underneath — secretly, at its foundation.

demolish vs. undermine

demolish vs. undermine: Demolish is the most violent of the four — it flattens something in one blow — while undermine works slowly and invisibly, removing support piece by piece until things collapse.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — under-

Prefix — under-: beneath, below (Old English)

Root — mine

Root — mine: to dig (Old French)

Put it together

Put it together: Under- means 'beneath' and mine means 'to dig' — undermining was originally a siege tactic of digging tunnels beneath a castle wall so it would collapse. Today it means weakening anything by quietly attacking its foundation.

Use the root in a new word: miner

Use the root in a new word: miner: The coal miner spent his shift digging tunnels deep underground — the same digging idea buried inside undermine.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Undermine is the word when something is being weakened from the inside or from its foundation, often secretly or gradually. Use it for authority, credibility, trust, or arguments being slowly eroded. For straightforward damage or direct attack, simpler words like 'weaken' or 'damage' are better choices.
